**The Imjin War (1592–1598)** – also known as the Japanese invasions of Korea – was a major conflict between the Japanese forces of Toyotomi Hideyoshi and the Korean Joseon dynasty, with Chinese Ming dynasty support. Here’s a concise overview: | Aspect | Details | |--------|---------| | **Timeframe** | 1592–1598 | | **Key Players** | • **Japan** – led by Toyotomi Hideyoshi, aiming to conquer Korea and then China.
• **Korea (Joseon)** – defended by King Seonjo and his generals.
• **China (Ming)** – intervened to protect the Ming dynasty’s southern border. | | **Causes** | • Hideyoshi’s ambition to expand Japanese influence.
• Desire to use Korea as a corridor to invade China.
• Korean refusal to allow Japanese troops to pass through. | | **Major Phases** | 1. **First Invasion (1592–1593)** – Japanese forces quickly captured Seoul and much of the peninsula.
2. **Korean & Ming Counter‑offensive (1593–1595)** – Korean navy (notably Admiral Yi Sun‑shin) and Ming troops pushed back Japanese forces.
3. **Second Invasion (1597–1598)** – Japanese attempted to regain lost territory but were ultimately defeated. | | **Key Battles** | • **Battle of Hansan Island** – Yi Sun‑shin’s naval victory using turtle ships.
• **Siege of Jinju** – Korean defenders held out against Japanese siege.
• **Battle of Noryang** – final naval engagement where Admiral Yi died. | | **Outcome** | • Japan withdrew after Hideyoshi’s death and internal strife.
• Korea suffered massive destruction, loss of life, and economic hardship.
• The war reinforced the importance of naval power and led to reforms in Korean military organization. | | **Legacy** | • The Imjin War is a pivotal event in East Asian history, shaping Korean national identity and military strategy.
